newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand worried about short-term foreign debt.
newsitem.headline: Thailand worried about short-term foreign debt.

text.p: A top finance ministry official said on Thursday he was concerned about the ratio of Thailand's short-term to long-term foreign debt.

"Thailand's current ratio of short-term to long-term foreign debts of 50/50 remains unsafe and risky because in other countries the short-term foreign debt accounts for only 30-40 percent of all foreign debt," ministry permanent secretary Chatumongkol Sonakul told reporters.
"The ratio must be improved to 40/60," he said.

He said that the Bank of Thailand was considering curbing short-term foreign borrowings by seeking an increase in the amount of lending to foreign borrowers through the Bangkok International Banking Facility.
But Chatumongkol said he disagreed with any plan to curb the import of short-term foreign funds by using tax measures because that could hinder foreign investment.
"Tax measures are not a good way to curb short-term foreign borrowings. If we impose tax, foreigners will be reluctant to invest (in Thailand)," he said.
